'Jouer à' for sports/games (jouer au foot), 'jouer de' for instruments (jouer de la guitare).
'Faire de' is used for many activities: faire du sport, faire de la natation (swimming), faire de l'équitation (horse riding).
souvent (often), toujours (always), parfois (sometimes), rarement (rarely), jamais (never, with ne).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 2: Popular Culture (Free-time Activities; Customs, Festivals and Celebrations; Celebrity Culture) — a core area of GCSE French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 2: Popular Culture (Free-time Activities; Customs, Festivals and Celebrations; Celebrity Culture) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 2: Popular Culture (Free-time Activities; Customs, Festivals and Celebrations; Celebrity Culture).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct way to say 'I play the guitar'?
options: Je joue de la guitare.
Je joue à la guitare.
Je fais la guitare.
Je joue la guitare.

mcqs.q: Which sentence means 'I played football yesterday'?
options: Hier, j'ai joué au foot.
Hier, je joue au foot.
Hier, je jouerai au foot.
Hier, je suis joué au foot.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I play the piano' vs 'I play football'?
options: Je joue le piano, je joue le football.
Je vais utiliser mon portable.
Je joue DU piano (instrument) vs je joue AU football (sport).
Same preposition for both - 'je joue piano', 'je joue football'.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I am using my phone right now' (emphasising the action is in progress)?
options: Je vais utiliser mon portable.
Je suis utilisant mon portable.
Christmas (the English word is used).
Je suis en train d'utiliser mon portable.

mcqs.q: What is the French word for 'Christmas'?
options: Je vais utiliser mon portable.
Noel.
Christmas (the English word is used).
Noël (with diaeresis on the ë).
